name: Rust
description: Rust: highlighting for the current editions, and rust-analyzer for completion, documentation, definitions, references, rename, diagnostics and formatting

rust-analyzer.name: rust-analyzer
rust-analyzer.install: rustup component add rust-analyzer; or brew install rust-analyzer; or a release from https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/releases, renamed rust-analyzer and put on the PATH

settings.rust-analyzer.checkOnSave.description: rust-analyzer: run the check command when a file is saved, its errors and warnings shown as diagnostics

settings.rust-analyzer.check.command.description: rust-analyzer: the Cargo command run on save: check, or clippy for its lints too (slower)

settings.rust-analyzer.check.extraArgs.description: rust-analyzer: more arguments for the check command, such as --locked

settings.rust-analyzer.check.allTargets.description: rust-analyzer: check tests, examples and benchmarks too (--all-targets); null for what cargo.allTargets says

settings.rust-analyzer.check.features.description: rust-analyzer: the features the check command turns on: "all", or a list of names; null for what cargo.features says

settings.rust-analyzer.check.workspace.description: rust-analyzer: check the whole workspace (--workspace), not only the package of the file saved

settings.rust-analyzer.cargo.features.description: rust-analyzer: the features turned on when it reads the project: "all", or a list of names

settings.rust-analyzer.cargo.noDefaultFe.description: rust-analyzer: leave the packages' default features off (--no-default-features)

settings.rust-analyzer.cargo.allTargets.description: rust-analyzer: read tests, examples and benchmarks too (--all-targets)

settings.rust-analyzer.cargo.targetDir.description: rust-analyzer: its own target folder, so that its builds and a cargo build in the terminal do not wait for each other: true for one under target/, or a path; null for the project's

settings.rust-analyzer.cargo.buildScript.description: rust-analyzer: run the packages' build scripts (build.rs), for the code they generate

settings.rust-analyzer.procMacro.enable.description: rust-analyzer: expand procedural macros (derives and attributes), which needs the build scripts run

settings.rust-analyzer.procMacro.ignored.description: rust-analyzer: procedural macros not expanded, by crate: {"crate": ["macro"]}

settings.rust-analyzer.completion.autoim.description: rust-analyzer: offer items not imported yet, the use added when one is taken

settings.rust-analyzer.completion.callab.description: rust-analyzer: what a completed function gets: its arguments as places to fill, its parentheses, or nothing (Kalem takes no snippets yet, so a function is completed by its name alone whatever this says)

settings.rust-analyzer.diagnostics.disab.description: rust-analyzer: its own diagnostics not shown, by code, such as unlinked-file or inactive-code

settings.rust-analyzer.diagnostics.exper.description: rust-analyzer: its experimental diagnostics too, which may be wrong more often

settings.rust-analyzer.files.exclude.description: rust-analyzer: files and folders it does not read, relative to the project

settings.rust-analyzer.rustfmt.extraArgs.description: rust-analyzer: more arguments for rustfmt when it formats a file

settings.rust-analyzer.rustfmt.overrideC.description: rust-analyzer: another formatter, as a program and its arguments that read the file on standard input (leptosfmt, a nightly rustfmt); null for rustfmt

settings.rust-analyzer.imports.granulari.description: rust-analyzer: how the imports it adds are grouped: one use per crate, per module, per item, one use for all, or as the file has them

settings.rust-analyzer.imports.prefix.description: rust-analyzer: how the paths it adds start: plain, with self, or with crate
